event.summary: Automatic start does not deadlock its own actor hold
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: Considered whether automatically starting a stopped container waits on the same connection actor and strands the container. Source refutation: manager.rs:3869-3875 spawns change_with_manager in a separate Tokio task; the actor then waits on next_nudge at 3879 and returns to the outer loop's hold/park acknowledgement at 3664-3673. environment/lifecycle.rs:69-80 takes the hold from that separate task, and manager.rs:1604-1643 sends a nudge and bounds parking. Thus the actor can acknowledge the lifecycle task instead of awaiting it inline. manager.rs:5156-5159 also refuses actor publication while a hold is active, so the task completion branch cannot replace an active lifecycle hold's display. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Disposable environments / Environment ownership and refusal, requires closing exec before pause and one actor-owned start; the source preserves the hold boundary. Suggested bucket: high if this deadlock existed; established impact none. Could-be-highest: false (this considered route concerns unavailable access, not established destruction or security). Confidence: confirmed by source only, no runtime execution. proposed_drop: refuted by the separate task and nudge/park path cited above. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this record checks self-deadlock/publication only; it does not establish every automatic-start episode behavior.

event.summary: Automatic-start self-deadlock remains refuted across hold and cancellation boundaries
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Synthesis revision preserves the original suspected consequence: an automatically started stopped container could become inaccessible if its actor awaited its own parking. Rechecked exact source: manager.rs:3866-3871 marks attempted before spawning an independent task with the upgraded manager; :3874-3881 races a borrowed JoinHandle against nudge/timer, so those select branches leave the handle in StoppedEpisode rather than aborting the lifecycle task. :3664-3670 acknowledges the current hold on the actor's next pass. hold_connection :1604-1644 publishes hold/client withdrawal before nudge and bounds parking. Actor publication refuses any hold (publish_refresh :5156-5159, previously checked). Dropping/resetting StoppedEpisode drops only a Tokio JoinHandle, documented at :3221-3228 as detachment; the operation owns its manager Arc and provision guard independently. The provider takes try_host_provision_lock before rereading binding (environment/podman.rs:649-670), so removal/retarget cannot change the resource under a start. The shared lifecycle perform :69-96 releases its hold after both success and ordinary returned errors, before its success retry await. Thus ordinary actor nudge, wait cancellation, or episode reset cannot cancel an acquired lifecycle hold halfway and does not create the proposed self-deadlock. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments requires one actor-owned attempt and closing exec before pause; owned lifecycle lifetime preserves that boundary. Suggested bucket if the original route existed: high; established impact none. Could-be-highest: false for this access/deadlock concern, without an established destruction/security route. Confidence: confirmed by source only, no runtime execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted for the self-deadlock/cancelled-wait route only, not accepted on behalf of the parent. possible_cover: none. Caveat: a provider panic or whole-runtime termination is not an ordinary cancellation path proven by this analysis; no evidence of a shipped panic trigger was found or claimed.

event.summary: Place listing does not synchronously probe every host
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: Considered whether opening the launcher waits for slow container-host probes. Source refutation: environment_places calls refresh in a loop, but environment/podman_probe.rs:435-476 only reads the current registry row, admits a deduplicated refresh and spawns the actual probe at 446; it returns immediately after spawning. Provider places at environment/podman.rs:952-975 reads cached view data only. Contract: SPEC.md, Container sessions, says 'A background probe records Linux, architecture, version and each requirement, with a timestamp' and 'Opening the launcher refreshes probes in the background. No per-host opt-in is needed, and an environment host cannot itself host containers.' SPEC_impl.md, Disposable environments / Podman places, creation and images, says 'No synchronous probe fan-out gates opening the launcher.' The awaited work here is local registry access rather than remote probe completion. Suggested bucket: high if remote fan-out blocked launch; established impact none. Could-be-highest: false. Confidence: confirmed by source only. proposed_drop: refuted by background spawn and cached projection cited above. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this checks blocking behavior; it does not assert a new probe is scheduled on every opening by this endpoint alone.

event.summary: Place-list probe fan-out remains background and cancellation-safe
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Synthesis revision preserves original suspected consequence: opening the launcher might block on multiple remote place probes. Rechecked environment/podman_probe.rs:435-475: the caller awaits a local registry read before admission, then inserts refreshing under a short std mutex and immediately spawns the owned probe, with no await between flag insertion and spawn. The task's Refreshing guard is installed before its first await (:447-455); its Drop removes the in-flight flag and notifies waiters (:479-494), including early returns and panic unwinding. Remote probe runs after the cache lock is released. Before publication it rereads the current row and requires the same route (:458-472); ordinary view also filters cached probes by route (:304-319). HTTP caller cancellation before the initial local read completes creates no remote task/flag, and cancellation after spawning does not own the spawned probe. Provider cached places and host listing remain as previously checked. No remote fan-out or retained cache mutex blocks launcher listing. Contract SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments / Podman places, creation and images: 'No synchronous probe fan-out gates opening the launcher.' Suggested bucket if original concern existed: high; established impact none. Could-be-highest: false. Confidence: confirmed from source only. proposed_drop: original blocking/cancellation concern is source-refuted; this is a proposed disposition, not a parent-accepted drop or a filter. possible_cover: none. Caveat preserved: this endpoint's missing-cache bootstrap does not by itself prove refresh is scheduled on every repeated opening; this record makes no claim about that distinct UI scheduling behavior, which is outside this blocking candidate.

A reset at that settled failure boundary could therefore escape the test. This is a test-oracle gap, not a claimed product failure. Source: stopped_autostart_is_owned_once_and_retains_failure_across_unanswered_reads (:13282-13338) switches provider reads to StatusUnanswered, waits for only two provider invocations (:13314-13316), then restores Stopped and calls Retry (:13317-13318). sandbox_fixture constructs a Tensorlake host with Cadence::default (:13037-13077); default connect_backoff has six waits and seven total attempts (:116-123,237-244). The scripted failed resume calls release_hold(host,true) (:13014), requesting an active retry window. In connect_phase (:3951-4020), individual AttemptOutcome::Failed values stay in the inner ladder; only after all seven failures does the outer actor receive Failed and execute its retention boundary (:3812-3817). A retry nudge during that ladder instead returns Interrupted (:3971-3977,3998-4001), never entering the Failed arm. Thus two unanswered observations can be the first two attempts of a single active cycle, after which the test itself interrupts it. source.status counts invocation before cloning its answer (:12979-12981); wait_for_checks watches only that count (:12912-12916), not outer failure settlement. The first start_failed publication occurs in the Stopped select result arm (:3883-3889); the release's fresh-window nudge and next row reload/connection attempt are separate scheduling boundaries, so the test can install its unanswered answer before the post-release active attempt. No invariant forces a completed Failed cycle before the two-count threshold. Competing mechanism: erroneously clearing StoppedEpisode only in the outer AttemptOutcome::Failed arm would still allow preservation across the two inner errors and the later Stopped assertion on this admitted interleaving, while rearming starts after an actual unavailable cycle in production. The test's current docstring/intent is one owned start with failure retained across unanswered reads; observing only inner read counts does not establish the outer state transition that enforces continued episode ownership. Require a settled Unreachable result for this host before restoring Stopped (or use an explicitly one-attempt cadence and observe its settled failure), then assert one start and retained failure. Keep the independent hold/self-deadlock and Suspended-reset checks. Contract: supplied Test authoring review requires establishing the fixture premise and an observable distinguishing competing mechanisms. Production state machine currently retains stopped state correctly; that does not refute the missing test premise. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer regression assurance).
